what.action: Phase 8 Phase A landed — Tapscript-style authorization tree primitives on the org self-declaration (commit 4eaeba8).
what.summary: selfDeclareOrganization extended with optional authRules parameter that emits an auth sub-branch in the claim tree. Each rule is one field-tree leaf carrying canonical JSON of {threshold, eligible}, eligible normalized to sorted-lowercased. Validation throws synchronously on duplicate action / threshold < 1 / non-integer threshold / threshold > eligible-set size. New exported helpers findAuthRule + listAuthRules + proveAuthorization; proveAuthorization wraps the shipped disclosureProof from tapit-attest/src/core/field-tree.ts to produce a DisclosureProofBundle that Phase B's verifier will consume. Zero new cryptographic code in tapit-attest; no library version bump. New test file ships 15 tests across three describe blocks; the load-bearing one forges a leaf-value in a proof bundle and confirms verifyDisclosureProof rejects it, proving the carried signature binds the proof to the original claim digest.

why.text: Operator authorized Phase A with 'Yes a please' after the prior session committed the canonical Tapscript-style brief. Phase A is the substrate-on-disk step — not yet a user-visible feature, but the load-bearing proof that the architectural argument from the brief compiles, type-checks, verifies its own cryptography under tamper, and integrates cleanly with the shipped disclosure-proof primitive. Every subsequent phase builds on a substrate that no longer has to be argued for from theory.

confidence.uncertainty: Phase A is a primitive cut with no user-visible UI. The substrate is provably on disk and the disclosure-proof round-trip survives the leaf-value forgery test, but the other three forgery classes (wrong-org-binding, tampered sibling-hash path, tampered meta-fields) are Phase B's verifier surface and have no test coverage yet.
